claim: With human nouns, which is possible only with nouns denoting infants without specification of sex.
evidence_summary: Ch. 12, p. 1048, “Two special cases of which used with human antecedents”: They accused him of being a traitor, which he undoubtedly was [44i], and complements of have (got) [45]. That passage refers back to §17.3.
finding: Restrict the claim to referential antecedents or cross-refer to Ch. 12, §3.5.1. Brett’s personhood paper discusses infants and the who/which split but not these cases.
proposed_wording: With referential human antecedents, which is possible only with nouns denoting infants … (but see Ch. 12, §3.5.1)
inference: Is which with a human antecedent limited to infant nouns?

evidence.establishes: An unqualified only conflicts with a later section that cites this one.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
